title: Akathist to the Most Holy Theotokos
subtitle: The original Akathist of the seventh century.
intro: Stand if you are able: the hymn is sung standing, which is what its name means. The opening Kontakion is given here as Isabel Hapgood printed it in 1906. The stanzas that follow it, twelve ikoi and twelve kontakia, are being set from a public-domain printing and checked line by line, and none is shown until it has been.
source: Isabel Florence Hapgood, Service Book of the Holy Orthodox-Catholic Apostolic (Greco-Russian) Church (Boston: Houghton Mifflin, 1906), public domain: the Akathist's opening Kontakion, which the volume prints in the Divine Liturgy celebrated by a Bishop (Cornell University Library copy, archive.org cu31924029363128, scan page 125).

prayers.title: Kontakion 1
prayers.text: We, thy servants, in that we have been delivered from calamity, do offer unto thee, O Birth-giver of God, who as a victorious Chieftain warrest for us, songs of triumph and thanksgiving. Do thou also, in that thou hast might invincible, free us from all assaults, that we may cry unto thee:
